title: Antony and Cleopatra
objective: After this level you can describe the alliance of Mark Antony and Cleopatra and why it alarmed Rome.
summary: Antony ruled the East and allied with Cleopatra, last of the Ptolemies. When he gave her Roman lands, Octavian called him a traitor.

cards.headline: A Roman general and an Egyptian queen formed a partnership Rome called treason.
cards.body: Mark Antony ran Rome’s East. Cleopatra ruled Egypt. Together they handed Octavian exactly the story he needed.

cards.headline: The last of the Ptolemies
cards.body: Cleopatra VII was the last active ruler of Egypt’s Ptolemaic dynasty. Egyptian throne, Greek family: the Ptolemies were Greek-speaking, descended from one of Alexander the Great’s generals. And Roman generals were nothing new to her. She had been Julius Caesar’s ally and lover, and had a son, Caesarion, whom she said was Caesar’s. So when Antony came along, she had done this before.

cards.headline: Antony goes East
cards.body: After Philippi, Antony took charge of Rome’s eastern provinces and allied with Cleopatra. There was a small complication: in 40 BCE he had married Octavian’s sister, Octavia. He later left her for Cleopatra. Then, in 34 BCE, came the Donations of Alexandria, when Antony gave Roman lands in the East to Cleopatra and her children. Leaving your partner’s sister is awkward. Giving away Roman land is something else.

cards.fact: Octavian turned the romance into a weapon.
cards.context: He painted Antony as a traitor under the spell of a foreign queen, a Roman handing Roman land to her family. It worked: opinion in Rome turned against Antony. Octavian didn’t need to invent a scandal. Antony had supplied one.
